title: Journalist & Whistleblower Privacy for Beginners
metaDescription: Essential privacy guide for journalists and whistleblowers. Learn source protection, secure communication, and operational security basics.
intro: Protecting sources and maintaining privacy is crucial for journalists and whistleblowers. This guide covers essential security practices to safeguard communications, protect identities, and maintain operational security in high-risk situations.
prerequisites: Understanding of email and messaging apps
Access to a smartphone or computer

steps.title: Understand Your Threat Model
steps.description: Identify what you need to protect, who you're protecting it from, and what resources they might have to compromise your security.
actions: List sensitive information you handle (sources, documents, communications)
Identify potential threats (government surveillance, hackers, legal pressure)
Assess your adversary's capabilities (technical skills, legal powers, resources)
Document your security priorities and acceptable risk levels
steps.proTip: Your threat model will evolve with each story. Reassess regularly and adjust your security practices accordingly.

steps.title: Secure Your Devices
steps.description: Implement basic device security to protect against physical access, malware, and unauthorized surveillance.
actions: Enable full disk encryption on all devices (FileVault on Mac, BitLocker on Windows)
Set strong passwords and enable two-factor authentication
Keep operating systems and software updated with latest security patches
Install reputable antivirus software and enable automatic scanning
steps.warning: Avoid using personal devices for sensitive work. Consider using dedicated devices for high-risk communications.

steps.title: Choose Secure Communication Tools
steps.description: Select messaging and communication platforms that offer end-to-end encryption and strong privacy protections.
actions: Install Signal for encrypted messaging and voice calls
Use ProtonMail or Tutanota for secure email communications
Consider Element (Matrix) for group communications with sources
Set messages to auto-delete after a reasonable time period
steps.proTip: Always verify encryption keys when communicating with new sources to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.

steps.title: Browse Anonymously
steps.description: Protect your online research and communications by masking your IP address and browsing patterns.
actions: Use Tor Browser for anonymous web browsing and research
Use a privacy-focused browser additional privacy features and ad blocking
Connect through a reputable VPN service when using regular browsers
Avoid logging into personal accounts while conducting sensitive research
steps.proTip: Combine Tor with a VPN for enhanced anonymity, but be aware this may slow down your connection significantly.

steps.title: Establish Secure Meeting Practices
steps.description: Implement operational security measures for in-person and virtual meetings with sources.
actions: Meet sources in public places with multiple exits and good cell coverage
Turn off devices or place them in Faraday bags to prevent location tracking
Use burner phones for initial contact and meeting coordination
Establish code words or phrases for emergency situations
steps.warning: Never meet sources at your home, office, or other locations that could compromise your identity or theirs.

steps.title: Secure Document Handling
steps.description: Protect sensitive documents and files throughout the entire reporting process from receipt to publication.
actions: Use encrypted cloud storage like SpiderOak or Tresorit for file backups
Implement SecureDrop or similar systems for anonymous document submission
Strip metadata from documents before sharing or publishing
Create encrypted archives of important files with strong passwords
steps.proTip: Always make multiple encrypted backups of critical documents and store them in different physical locations.

steps.title: Prepare for Legal and Physical Threats
steps.description: Develop contingency plans for device seizure, legal compulsion, and other security incidents.
actions: Create a media security plan with your legal team or press freedom organization
Practice quickly wiping devices and logging out of accounts
Establish dead man's switches for critical information
Know your legal rights regarding source protection in your jurisdiction
steps.warning: Legal protections for journalists vary by country and may not protect against all forms of government pressure.

pro_tips: Use different pseudonyms and communication methods for different sources to compartmentalize your security risks.
Regularly audit your digital footprint by searching for your name and associated information online.
Consider using cash-purchased prepaid phones and gift cards for anonymous communications and services.
Join press freedom organizations like Freedom of the Press Foundation for ongoing security training and legal support.
Practice your security procedures regularly, including emergency protocols, to ensure you can execute them under pressure.

faqs.question: Is it legal to use encryption and anonymity tools as a journalist?
faqs.answer: In most democratic countries, journalists have the legal right to use encryption and privacy tools to protect their sources. However, laws vary by jurisdiction, so consult with press freedom lawyers in your area.

faqs.question: How do I know if my communications are being monitored?
faqs.answer: It's often difficult to detect surveillance. Look for unusual device behavior, unexpected battery drain, or suspicious network activity. Assume you're being monitored if you're working on sensitive stories involving powerful interests.

faqs.question: What should I do if law enforcement seizes my devices?
faqs.answer: Immediately contact your legal counsel and press freedom organizations. Do not provide passwords or encryption keys without legal advice. Having a predetermined legal response plan is crucial.

faqs.question: Can I use regular social media for source communications?
faqs.answer: No. Platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram are not secure for sensitive communications. They collect extensive metadata and can be compelled to turn over data to authorities.

faqs.question: How do I verify if a source is legitimate and not a trap?
faqs.answer: Take time to verify sources through multiple channels, check their claims against known facts, and be wary of sources offering information that seems too good to be true. Trust your instincts and proceed cautiously.
